name: Electronic Visa (e-Visa) / Visa-Free Entry

requirements.blocker_text: Arab League member-state nationals may enter federal Iraq visa-free for 30 days with an ordinary passport; select diplomatic/service passport holders get exemptions up to 6 months. As of 1 March 2025, Iraq discontinued visa-on-arrival for most other nationalities -- they must obtain an e-Visa in advance, costing approximately $160. Journalists and NGO workers cannot use the e-Visa system at all and must apply through an embassy instead. Israeli nationals are banned outright, including transit and layovers.
requirements.fix_path: Arab League nationals enter visa-free for 30 days; others must obtain an e-Visa (~$160) before travel, except journalists/NGO workers, who must apply through a diplomatic mission.

requirements.blocker_text: The Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) runs its OWN e-visa platform, separate from federal Iraq's. Citizens of certain countries can get a visa on arrival at Erbil or Sulaymaniyah airports (30 days) or Kirkuk airport (60 days for some nationalities); others must use a local sponsor to obtain a KRI e-visa, priced at 100,000 IQD (slightly cheaper than federal Iraq's e-Visa). A specific list of nationalities (including Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Ethiopia, Guatemala, Kenya, Nigeria, Somalia, Uganda, Yemen) cannot obtain KRI e-visas independently and need a sponsor.
requirements.fix_path: Check eligibility for KRI visa-on-arrival at Erbil/Sulaymaniyah/Kirkuk; otherwise apply for the KRI e-visa (100,000 IQD), arranging a local sponsor if required by nationality.

outcome.duration_length: 30 days (Arab League visa-free, KRI visa-on-arrival) or 60 days (Kirkuk, select nationalities)

sources.title: Wikipedia -- federal e-Visa system (since March 2025), Arab League exemption, separate Kurdistan Region e-visa/visa-on-arrival system

STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to Wikipedia, tier 4; Iraq's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (mofa.gov.iq, reached successfully for the citizenship files in this same build) does not appear to publish a full visa-policy page, and the Ministry of Justice's own PDF hosting (moj.gov.iq) timed out on this specific document. MARQUEE STRUCTURAL FINDING, the central theme of this country's build: Iraq runs TWO PARALLEL immigration systems -- the federal government's (Baghdad) and the Kurdistan Regional Government's (Erbil) -- with separate e-visa platforms, separate visa-on-arrival rules, and, as this country's other files show, a separate KRG investor-visa pathway with no clear federal equivalent found. This dual-track structure is comparable in spirit to Bosnia's state/entity duality (ba_citizenship_naturalisation.json) but here it runs through the ENTIRE immigration system, not just citizenship. GENUINE, CURRENT FINDING: federal Iraq eliminated visa-on-arrival for most nationalities as of March 2025, a relatively recent tightening.
